recommendedActions: Monitor for device code phishing activity and respond per Microsoft Defender for Office 365 guidance
Revoke compromised user’s refresh tokens using revokeSign-inSessions API
Implement Conditional Access policies enforcing re‑authentication for users
Temporarily disable compromised accounts to contain token abuse
Enable Microsoft Defender for Office 365 pre-d delivery protection against device code phishing
Implement email filtering rules that flag URLs and QR codes pointing to Microsoft authentication endpoints via social engineering lures
Monitor Azure app registrations and block anomalous client ID usage in OAuth flows
Use threat intelligence feeds to block domains associated with SquarePhish and Graphish kit
Implement URL filtering to block suspicious Cloudflare Worker domains
Verify the authenticity of cloud storage links before interacting with them
campaignsText: TA2723 has launched several high‑volume campaigns since October 2025, primarily targeting Microsoft 365 users through malicious OAuth Device Code flows. The actor employs a distributed architecture that allows rapid code generation and clipboard hijacking across thousands of victims simultaneously. Victims include multiple sectors—government agencies, defense contractors, universities, transportation companies, and financial institutions—across Brazil, Mexico, Iran, China, Russia, Ukraine, and the United States. Notable past operations involved large‑scale token theft that enabled lateral movement within corporate networks and facilitated exfiltration of sensitive data. The group uses compromised high‑profile email addresses and AI‑generated lures to increase spearphishing success rates. Operational tempo is aggressive: accounts are compromised in a matter of minutes through short‑lived device codes, tokens are harvested instantly, and lateral exploitation can occur before the victim notices an anomalous login activity.
description: TA2723 (also known as Storm‑2372, BokBot, and UNK_AcademicFlare) is a financially motivated actor that runs large‑volume credential phishing campaigns focused on Microsoft’s OAuth Device Code flow. The group spoofs OneDrive and other cloud services using Cloudflare Workers and AI‑generated spearphishing lures to harvest device codes, bypass MFA limits, and obtain valid access tokens for account takeover. Once in an M365 environment, attackers can exfiltrate data and pivot laterally.
goals: TA2723 is driven primarily by financial gain. Its strategy involves acquiring valuable credentials to monetize via direct data theft, sale of stolen accounts, or ransomware deployments in targeted sectors. The actor selects victims with high information value—especially those using Microsoft cloud services—and tailors spearphishing campaigns to resonate with the target’s operational context (e.g., academic settings for universities, maritime logistics for transportation). By leveraging compromised government addresses and embedding QR codes that redirect to legitimate authentication endpoints, TA2723 increases perceived authenticity and reduces suspicion among victims.
